info.title: webority-db-migrator - shared schema runner (DbUp), SQL Server or PostgreSQL
info.description: Shared DbUp-based schema runner for every Webority database project, SQL Server or PostgreSQL. Run-once journaled Scripts/ + StoredProcedures/ re-applied when changed, tracked in dbo.SchemaVersions on SQL Server and public.SchemaVersions on PostgreSQL, both stamped in UTC with a content checksum.

options.name: --connection
options.description: Connection string (or set MIGRATOR_CONNECTION env var)

options.name: --db-root
options.description: DB project folder with Scripts/ and/or StoredProcedures/ (default: .)

options.name: --what-if
options.description:
List pending run-once scripts, run the applied-script guard below,
and exit. Changes nothing.

options.name: --mark-applied
options.description: Baseline: record existing run-once scripts as applied WITHOUT executing

options.name: --force
options.description:
Allow --mark-applied against a DB whose journal already has entries
(only valid with --mark-applied)

options.name: --tx-per-script
options.description: Wrap each script in its own transaction (default: off)

options.name: --accept-checksum
options.description:
Accept the current content of one already-applied script (repeatable)
That rewrites the stored hash for that one script from the file on disk, printing the old and new
values. There is deliberately no switch to turn the guard off everywhere.
Stored procedures:
Each StoredProcedures/ file's content is hashed into SchemaVersionsRunAlways after it runs. A file
whose hash still matches is skipped. Every procedure runs when a run-once script is pending in
the same run, on the first run of this version (the table starts empty), and with
--reapply-procedures. A procedure edited or dropped by hand on the server is not put back until
one of those happens.
What the command line will not accept:
A bare word with no option in front of it, so a connection string passed without --connection
stops the run instead of being dropped in favour of MIGRATOR_CONNECTION. A value that is itself
an option, so --connection --what-if is a typo rather than a connection string. --force without
--mark-applied, which is the only thing it relaxes. --what-if together with --mark-applied,
which ask for opposite things. --reapply-procedures with --mark-applied or with --lint alone,
neither of which runs a procedure.
Exit codes:
0  success
1  migration failure
2  usage/config error

options.name: --reapply-procedures
options.description:
Run every stored procedure, changed or not. With --what-if, the
preview shows them all as pending.

options.name: --lint
options.description:
Lint the PENDING run-once scripts against the script conventions and
exit 1 on any error. Changes nothing. With --what-if, the preview lints too.

options.name: --report-json
options.description:
With --lint: write the pending scripts and the findings
to a JSON file

options.name: --help
options.description:
Show this help and exit
The lint (pending scripts only):
Errors: a CREATE TABLE, ADD column or CREATE INDEX with no guard; DROP TABLE/COLUMN, ALTER COLUMN
to a new type, TRUNCATE, or DELETE/UPDATE with no WHERE and no matching *_Rollback.sql; a file
name timestamp that is malformed or sorts before the newest applied script; ADD ... NOT NULL
with no DEFAULT. Warning (SQL Server): CREATE INDEX without ONLINE = ON.
Waive one finding with a comment on or above its line, the reason being required:
-- lint:allow destructive-no-rollback table was never populated
The applied-script guard:
Every run-once script's content is hashed into SchemaVersions.Checksum when it is applied. On a
later run, a script whose content no longer matches its stored hash fails the run, because an
applied script is immutable by convention and an edit to one is silently ignored on every
database that already ran it. Stored procedures are never refused by it.
Line endings and a trailing newline are ignored, so the same script on Windows and Linux agrees.
